name: JK Simpson 5-String Banjo
description: A quite rare and hard to find banjo in fine condition. Features a Walrus tailpiece.

name: JK Simpson 7-String Banjo
description: Very rare 7-string example with daisy pattern tuners and scrim ware tailpiece (likely Walrus). Fine condition throughout.

name: Etherington Haymarket Fretless Banjo
description: A beautifully made fretless banjo of the highest quality. A rare instrument in this fine original condition.

name: GC Dobson Victor Banjo
description: All information including serial number and patent dates is stamped on the perch pole. A hard to find model in fine condition, and a gem to play.

name: Unmarked Stratton Banjo
description: Unmarked example attributed to John F. Stratton of New York. These banjos were retailed by Stratton & Son and almost certainly manufactured for them by J.H. Buckbee. No visible markings — typical of Stratton's unbranded instruments. In fine condition and a gem to play.

name: Wright’s “Challenger” 5‑String Banjo
description: An exceptional‑quality late‑19th‑century five‑string instrument – Wright’s “Challenger”, possibly crafted by Matthew Wright or made for J. Daniels. Beautiful rosewood neck (also described as king‑wood), engraved pot 12 inches diameter, scale length 28 inches. Finished with a fine scrimshaw tailpiece – appearing walrus‑ivory – another outstanding antique banjo.

name: Walter Taylor Liverpool 5‑String Banjo
description: Fine late‑19th‑century five‑string banjo crafted by Walter Taylor of Liverpool. Originally a gun‑smith, Taylor brought incredible skill, precision and finish to every instrument — his banjos are famous for outstanding build‑quality, beautiful laminated work and wonderful decorative inlays. Features a 12‑inch pot and scale length of 26 ½ inches; completely original and untouched throughout.

name: J. Daniels Piccolo Banjo
description: Fine late‑19th‑century piccolo‑size banjo made by J. Daniels, dating roughly 1878 – 1880. Very compact proportions: 7‑inch pot diameter, scale length 16 ½ inches, and a complete overall length of just 21 ½ inches.

name: Six‑String Tunbridge‑Ware Style Banjo
description: Fine high‑quality six‑string banjo made roughly 1865 – 1870. Beautifully crafted marquetry / patterned inlaid neck — very likely a genuine Tunbridge‑ware example. Pot diameter measures 11 ½ inches throughout; a wonderful, decorative instrument of exceptional quality.

name: 7‑String Banjo – Unknown Maker
description: Rare and beautifully‑made high‑grade seven‑string banjo dating to the late 1800s; maker currently unidentified. Fine detailing includes decorative maple stringing inlaid along the neck edges; pot 12 inches, scale length 29 inches. Fittings – hooks, shoes and nut – were originally gold‑plated; they have been professionally cleaned, stabilised and remain intact.

name: Quality 5‑String Banjo – 1930s
description: Fine‑quality five‑string banjo made during the 1930s. Strong three‑piece neck construction; 11‑inch pot featuring a countersunk tone‑ring set neatly within a wood rim. Scale length 25 inches — a splendid, well‑made instrument throughout.

name: T.W.Bacon Flush-Fret 5-String Banjo
description: Fine late-19th-century five-string banjo by T.W.Bacon, made around 1882. 11½-inch pot with integral rolled tone-ring; scale length 27 inches. Distinctive flush-set frets crafted from ivory or bone — beautifully finished and a classic example of Bacon's high-grade work.

name: Early English Banjo, c.1850
description: A truly rare and important early English banjo, dating to approximately 1850 — the earliest example in this collection. It remains fully playable, yet stands equally as a magnificent decorative piece and authentic antique. The neck features exquisite inlay work in Mother‑of‑Pearl, semi‑precious stones, and German Silver — a fascinating and unusual alloy that contains no actual silver, making this detail a wonderful point of historical interest. A truly unique piece of early banjo‑making history.
